title: First Trimester Nutrition Checklist: Folate, Iron, and Safer Foods
excerpt: Prioritize folic acid, iron-rich foods, hydration, and cooked foods during weeks 1–12
content:
## Introduction
During the first trimester of pregnancy, nutrition plays a crucial role in the development of the fetus. Providing adequate essential nutrients will help the fetus develop healthily and reduce the risk of diseases. In this article, we will explore the key aspects of nutrition during the first trimester, including folate, iron, and safer foods.

## Folate and its role
Folate is a crucial B vitamin that plays a primary role in fetal development. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), folate helps prevent neural tube defects in the fetus. To provide adequate folate, pregnant women should consume folate-rich foods such as leafy greens, fruits, and dairy products.

## Iron and its importance
Iron is another essential nutrient during the first trimester of pregnancy. Iron helps produce red blood cells, providing oxygen to the fetus and preventing anemia. Pregnant women should consume iron-rich foods such as red meat, chicken, fish, and legumes.

## Safer foods and cooking methods
During the first trimester of pregnancy, pregnant women should prioritize safer foods and cooking methods. Foods like raw meat, raw eggs, and raw fish can contain harmful bacteria like Salmonella and Listeria. To ensure safety, pregnant women should cook these foods thoroughly before consumption.

## Cooking and food storage
To ensure food safety, pregnant women should follow these guidelines:
- Cook foods thoroughly before consumption
- Store foods at suitable temperatures
- Avoid consuming expired or spoiled foods

## Conclusion
Nutrition during the first trimester of pregnancy is vital. Pregnant women should prioritize folate-rich foods, iron-rich foods, and cooked foods to ensure the healthy development of the fetus. To learn more about prenatal nutrition, you can visit our [meal planner](/planner) page.

## Note
Before making any changes to their diet, pregnant women should consult their doctor or a registered dietitian to ensure safety and effectiveness.

faqs.question: Why is folate important during the first trimester of pregnancy?
faqs.answer: Folate helps prevent neural tube defects in the fetus.

faqs.question: How can I ensure adequate iron intake during the first trimester of pregnancy?
faqs.answer: Pregnant women should consume iron-rich foods such as red meat, chicken, fish, and legumes.

faqs.question: Why is it important to cook foods thoroughly during the first trimester of pregnancy?
faqs.answer: Cooking foods thoroughly helps prevent the risk of foodborne illnesses caused by bacteria like Salmonella and Listeria.
